grades.quote: Each entry can contain the extent’s length and starting disk block number. In the example, the two extent map entries would be (40 _,_ 1000) and (30 _,_ 1200). These say the file contains 40 blocks starting at disk block 1000 and 30 blocks starting at disk block 1200.
grades.reason: Substantively explains extent maps, a compact alternative to storing every data-block address individually, and discusses their storage in inodes or B+-trees.
Discusses inode allocation, locking, and reclamation, not representation of block addresses that exceed inode capacity.

grades.quote: For larger files, these file systems keep the inodes compact by using indirect blocks, roughly analogous to multilevel page tables.
grades.reason: Directly answers that larger files use indirect blocks, and also identifies extent maps and B+-trees as alternatives.
Only describes exposing inode metadata through stat; it does not address data-block mapping.
